newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singtel says room for four phone firms.
newsitem.headline: Singtel says room for four phone firms.

text.p: Singapore has room for four competing telecommunications companies, the chairman of the country's current monopoly said on Thursday.
"I think there will probably be room for four competitors," Koh Boon Hwee, chairman of Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel), told reporters.
The number of phone users and the potential demand for extra lines and services between now and 2000 would provide good business opportunities for several companies, Koh said.
Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan said on Wednesday that four providers, including cellular operators, was the maximum Singapore would give licences as it deregulated the industry.
"There is a case to have up to four licences but we reserve the right to have only one more. Four will be the maximum for the foreseeable future," Mah told reporters.
SingTel loses its monopoly status on April 1 when new cellular operator, MobileOne, begins business.
MobileOne is a consortium comprising Keppel Telecom, Singapore Press Holdings, Cable & Wireless and Hong Kong Telecommunications.
SingTel was looking forward to the competition and was confident of retaining the majority of its existing cellular subscribers, Koh said.
It was no surprise that MobileOne's initial strategy appeared to be based on offering low prices, he added.
"I don't believe it to be a surprising strategy. From a business point of view it's a very rational strategy," Koh said.
